checks.what: Library size: the article states 'a combinatorial library of 100 unique ionizable lipids (AMG) by combining 10 amine headgroups (Am), 9 glycidyl esters and 1 epoxy-ester tails (G)' and 'we then synthesized and purified (>90% purity) all 100'.
Each reconstructed structure against the HRMS m/z printed beside it in the SI, as [M+H]+ or [M+2H]2+, gate 25 ppm.
Each building block is re-derived independently from every lipid that contains it; all reads of one block must give the same graph.
Blocks re-assembled with curation/lib/assemble must reproduce the drawn molecule exactly (canonical SMILES identity).
checks.stereo_waiver_reason: assemble.check_stereo_preserved refuses a bond that CREATES a stereocentre; waived only where neither fragment nor product carries a single ASSIGNED centre, so nothing can be inverted

checks.what: 'AMG1541 ... features a hexacyclen headgroup (Am15)' (Conclusions). Am15 is derived here only from AMG1541's and AMG15L-41's drawings.
'... and monounsaturated 12 carbon tails' (Conclusions). G41's acyl chain, counted from the graph, not from the name token '41'.
'Within the tails we included Z-alkenes ...' (Results). Geometry read from the drawing's own coordinates, not assumed.
'... 9 glycidyl esters and 1 epoxy-ester tails (G)'. A glycidyl ester opens at the glycidyl CH2, so its arm reads CH2-CH(OH)-CH2-O-C(=O); the epoxy ester does not.

'AMG1541 LNPs exhibit 8.3-fold lower expression in the liver (Figure 2f)'. Figure 2f's two Source Data columns are UNLABELLED; the ratio identifies them -- column 1 / column 2 = the printed value, so column 1 is SM-102 and column 2 is AMG1541.
'... 3.5-fold higher expression at the injection site relative to SM-102 (Figure 2c)'.
'Systematic optimization ... identified AMG1541 which gave 4.5-fold higher mRNA expression than our initial hit, AMG104'. Figure 5c's own 'Fold Luciferase (AMG 104)' column.
'LNPs formulated with AMG1541-OHD exhibited ~100-fold loss in IM FLuc expression (Figure 5f)'.
'AMG1559 ... showed a dramatic 34-fold drop in transfection (Extended Figure 5d)'.
The per-lipid n printed in each figure legend against the number of values the publisher's Source Data actually contains for that lipid. 27 statements, each naming a specific lipid.
'The purity of all AMG lipids was >=90% as judged by LC-MS' (SI p.5) against every 'LC-MS purity' value printed in the SI.
'We found that >80 LNPs showed strong in vitro transfection' (Extended Figure 1). The article gives no threshold, so the count is reported against several and the claim is NOT scored.

'We chose to generate batches based on the tail structure, as this had the largest effect on mRNA delivery in vitro (Extended Figure 1)'. One-way variance explained in log10(RFU) by the tail and by the headgroup. This is also the ORIENTATION check on the 10 x 10 matrix: transposing rows and columns would put all 100 values on the wrong lipids and would swap these two numbers, and nothing else here would notice.

value_tier: 1_publisher_source_data for every value; no pixel was read anywhere in this curation
